However, direct momentum-resolved experimental evidence of their impact on quasiparticle electronic structure remains scarce, particularly in nitride semiconductors. Here, we present conclusive experimental evidence of electron-phonon interaction-induced quasiparticle renormalization and pronounced spectral broadening in p-type scandium nitride (ScN), using soft x-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. First-principles spectral-function calculations due to electron-phonon coupling reproduce the measured spectra, capturing a pronounced quasiparticle kink ~2.3 eV below the valence-band maximum, phonon satellite features arising from long-range electron-phonon coupling, and a direct bandgap zero-point renormalization of -124.3 meV within the non-adiabatic Allen-Heine-Cardona approach. We further show that the anomalous temperature-induced increase in the direct bandgap in ScN originates from the combined effects of thermal expansion and electron-phonon coupling, contributing comparably near room temperature. Our results establish ScN as a model platform for visualizing electron-phonon coupling and provide a quantitative benchmark for predictive first-principles descriptions of quasiparticle renormalization in semiconductors.

title: Finite-step projective dynamics of Schrödinger cocycles: non-degeneracy, regularity, and rigidity
summary:
We study the no deterministic images condition (NDI) for Schrödinger cocycles, which excludes a common image of a fixed probability measure under almost all projective transfer transformations. We prove two-step NDI at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and ergodic potentials with infinite essential range, and classify persistence for finite-state locally constant potentials. For bounded Markov and hidden Markov potentials on general state spaces under a one-step $L^2$ norm gap condition on the Markov operator, we prove Hölder bounds for solution-direction distributions above an exponential cutoff and Hölder conditional stationary measures. Counterexamples show the essential sharpness of both assumptions.
  For nonconstant real trigonometric potentials, including the almost Mathieu operator, we prove NDI and Hölder bounds for distributions of solution directions at all steps $k\ge2$ and all frequencies (rational or irrational). The exponent depends on the step, while the constant is uniform in steps, frequency and energy on compact intervals. For every irrational frequency and every energy with positive Lyapunov exponent, we prove non-atomicity of both Oseledets direction distributions and convergence to the unstable distribution from every phase-independent initial probability. This gives a new criterion for a zero Lyapunov exponent: a subsequential limit with an atom for one fixed initial direction suffices. All these results extend to an analytic class, with step-dependent regularity bounds.

title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
summary: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.

title: Quantum Field Theory on the Tangent Bundle
comment: 36 pages, to be submitted for publishing
summary: We develop a quantum-field-theoretical framework on the tangent bundle in which gravitational and internal gauge structures are associated with different sectors of an affine tangent-fiber geometry. The translational sector supplies the coframe and its relation to teleparallel gravity. A reduced vertical spectral problem is based on the centrally extended Euclidean group \(E^{c}(2)\), motivated by projective representations of the stabilizer of a nonzero null vector. Twofold multiplicities of equivalent vertical representations in selected left-chiral sectors admit weak \(SU(2)\) actions, while an assumed threefold quark multiplicity admits a locally gauged color \(SU(3)_c\) symmetry. A proposed global quotient correlates the color center with vertical rotations on a threefold rotation cover. Together with the selected chiral spectrum and anomaly conditions, this construction reproduces the observed fractional quark charge assignments. We formulate matter and gauge-field quantization, BRST symmetry, and anomaly constraints. Under the stated projection assumptions, the color sector has the standard local QCD structure, including its one-loop beta function and asymptotic freedom. Additional gauge bosons and dark-matter states are proposed as hypothetical sectors. We also formulate a structural action for possible couplings between teleparallel torsion and additional Lorentz-sector potentials. The framework relates selected structures of particle physics and gravity within a common geometric setting; their further dynamical and phenomenological development remains open.

title: Effect of Size Asymmetry and Zwitterionic Character of Solvent Ions on Impedance Spectra of Ultradilute Colloidal Suspensions
summary: Buffer chemistry modulates colloidal impedance critically for label-free biosensing and electrokinetic diagnostics, yet classical models neglect buffer-specific interactions. We studied carboxylated polystyrene (PS) microspheres in conductivity-matched zwitterionic 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid (HEPES) and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Two concentration-dependent regimes emerged: oscillatory at ultradilute concentrations (<0.02 w/v%; Region 1) and monotonic at higher concentrations (Region 2). In Region 1, HEPES at pH 6.9 (approximately 80% zwitterionic) produced the largest deviation of delta Z from the O'Brien prediction. The conductivity increment was opposite in sign to classical expectation. We attribute this to zwitterion-driven interfacial ordering that enhances local conductivity and promotes self-limiting particle clustering. Dynamic light scattering detected cluster formation at 0.008 w/v%, well below aggregation thresholds. Changing pH from 6.9 to 8.1 strongly altered impedance amplitude; DLS profiles remained invariant. This indicates zwitterions modulate electrochemical polarization, not physical assembly. Molecular dynamics simulations showed pH-dependent HEPES organization at the PS surface. At pH 6.9, interfacial charge- and number-density profiles showed comparable oscillatory periodicity. At pH 8.1, anionic HEPES produced a more diffuse profile with increased Na+ compensation. These results support interfacial ordering as a contributor to enhanced conductivity but do not establish discrete layers or registry. Zeta potentials distinguished stable HEPES interfaces from PBS, where magnitude increased with ionic strength, contrary to classical screening theory. These nonlinear signatures and mesoscale organization underscore the role of buffer selection in high-sensitivity impedance biosensing.

title: Curvature-induced fracture mode coupling in doubly curved shells
summary: Classical shell fracture theories predominantly consider cracks aligned with principal curvature directions in cylindrical and spherical shells under tensile mode or pressure loading, leaving the fracture behavior of arbitrarily oriented cracks in doubly curved shells under general loading poorly understood. Here, we introduce a semi-analytical framework based on Reissner shallow-shell theory to investigate isotropic shells with positive, zero, and negative Gaussian curvature. The formulation computes stress intensity factors, energy release rates, and crack-lip displacements for arbitrarily inclined through-thickness cracks in spheres, ellipsoids, cylinders, hyperboloids, and minimal surfaces under general mechanical loading. We show that shell curvature couples opening, sliding, and tearing, allowing a single loading component to activate multiple fracture modes, unlike in flat plates. This coupling depends strongly on crack orientation and the normal, parallel, and torsional components of the shell curvature. Ellipsoids exhibit weak coupling, hyperboloids generally exhibit the strongest coupling, and cylinders display the most complex orientation-dependent responses. Moreover, in-plane shear can induce crack closure in hyperboloidal shells, suggesting a potential geometric mechanism for enhanced damage resistance. These findings elucidate the role of local curvature in fracture-mode coupling and provide a mechanistic foundation for the analysis of shellular (meta-)structures with engineered curvature distributions.

title: From Specific Heat Bounds to Penrose-like Inequalities: A Unified Thermodynamic Perspective
summary: Under explicit and physically motivated assumptions, we identify a local-to-global thermodynamic mechanism that organizes several previously disconnected inequalities on black holes. We first focus on asymptotically flat, static, and spherically-symmetric black holes, and provide a unified thermodynamic perspective on various Penrose-like inequalities. We also discuss the generalizations in asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes/branes. In holographic settings, these bounds imply monotonic behavior of normalized thermodynamic quantities in the dual field theory. Notably, one central integrated inequality can be established directly under the NEC in general static planar symmetric asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black branes. Our purpose is not to claim a fully general proof of the proposed local bounds, but to expose a unified structural perspective connecting local thermodynamic constraints to global geometric inequalities. Establishing the local bounds beyond the classes considered here remains an open problem.

title: How to get an attractive model
summary: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: First-order magnetostructural transition in Ni-Mn-Sn powder - A matter of particle and grain size
summary: In Ni-Mn-based Heusler alloys, the magnetocaloric effect originates from a first-order magnetostructural transition (FOMST). However, the influence of particle and grain size on thermal hysteresis, transition width, and nucleation and growth mechanism remains poorly understood, as mechanical grinding can introduce residual stresses and processing-induced defects. In this study, we examined the size dependence of the FOMST in gas-atomized Ni-Mn-Sn powder by combining microstructural characterization with temperature-dependent XRD, magnetometry, calorimetry and single-particle measurements, enabling decoupling of size dependence from processing-related influences. We observed a pronounced size dependence of the transition ranges (Ms-Mf) and (Af-As), which decrease with decreasing particle size and approach zero for single-crystalline particles below ~20-30 micrometer. The thermal hysteresis decreases with increasing particle size, reaching a lower limit of 17 K for large polycrystalline particles above 100 micrometer. EBSD reveals a nearly constant grain size, implying a transition from polycrystalline to single-crystalline particles as particle size decreases. In polycrystalline particles, multiple grains transform gradually over an extended temperature interval because grain boundaries act as barriers to the progression of transformation. In contrast, single-grain particles lack preferred nucleation sites, resulting in larger hysteresis, while the absence of barriers to transformation propagation causes the entire particle to transform in a narrow range. These results demonstrate that the size dependence of the FOMST is governed by the interplay between particle size, grain boundaries, and the free particle surface.

title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
summary: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.

title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures and Periodic Orbits of Charged Particles Around a Five-Dimensional Rotating Black Hole: Comparison with the Kerr Black Hole
summary: We study periodic orbits of charged particles in the equatorial plane of a five-dimensional ($D=5$) rotating Myers--Perry black hole (BH) immersed in a uniform magnetic field, and the gravitational waves emitted by these orbits in an extreme mass-ratio inspiral. All results are compared with the Kerr BH in the uniform magnetic field. We find that a charged particle is much more weakly bound to the $D=5$ dimensional BH, i.e. its energy at the innermost stable circular orbit is close to unity, $0.95$--$0.99$, compared with $0.78$--$0.94$ for the Kerr BH, and the depth of the potential well is several times smaller. As a result, the periodic orbits of the $D=5$ dimensional BH lie much closer to the separatrix. The magnetic field can make the azimuthal frequency of the orbit smaller than the radial one and produces loops in the orbits far from the BH. Using the numerical kludge method, we compute the gravitational waveforms for a compact object of $10M_\odot$ orbiting a BH of $10^6M_\odot$. At the same magnetic field, the $D=5$ dimensional signal has a longer period, lower frequencies, and an amplitude smaller by about $18\%$. We show that for the magnetic parameter $βM=0.02$ the strongest spectral line is at $7.9$\,mHz, compared with $9.9$\,mHz for the Kerr BH. An estimate of the radiation reaction shows that the periodic orbits survive from less than an hour to a few days in the presence of an external magnetic field. Over these lifetimes, the signal-to-noise ratio for LISA is $7$--$31$ for the rotating BH in $D=5$ dimensions, compared to the Kerr BH where it is about $15$--$54$.

title: Quantum Reversibility Meets Classical Reverse Diffusion
comment: 12+16 pages, 1 figure, This is published version
summary: Bayes' rule connects forward and reverse processes in classical probability theory, and its quantum analogue has been discussed in terms of the Petz (transpose) map. For quantum dynamics governed by the Lindblad equation, the corresponding Petz map can also be written in Lindblad form. In classical stochastic systems, the analogue of the Lindblad equation is the Fokker-Planck equation, and applying Bayes' rule to it yields the reverse diffusion equation underlying modern diffusion-based generative models. It is known that a semiclassical approximation of the Lindblad equation yields the Fokker-Planck equation for the Wigner function, which is a quasiprobability distribution defined on phase space as the Wigner transform of the density operator. Here we demonstrate that applying the same approximation to the Lindblad equation associated with the Petz map produces an equation that coincides with that obtained from the Fokker-Planck equation via Bayes' rule. This finding establishes a direct correspondence between the Petz map and Bayes' rule, unifying quantum reversibility with classical reverse diffusion.

title: Exact Magnetic Confinement of a Doped Hole by Kinetic Frustration
summary: We establish an exact mechanism of magnetic confinement driven purely by kinetic frustration. In a finite open sawtooth $U=\infty$ Hubbard chain of $L$ unit cells doped with one hole, the ground state at magnetization $M$ contains $M$ polarized triplet dimers surrounding a connected singlet region of length $\ell_{\rm s}=L-M$. A magnetic field selects $M$ and hence the confinement length. The hole forms a standing wave in the singlet region with exponential tails in the triplet background. Confinement requires neither disorder nor an exchange-generated string tension: destructive interference between direct and apex-mediated hopping makes the triplet bonds reflecting. At $t_2/t_1=[2+4\cos(π/(\ell_{\rm s}+2))]^{-1/2}$, they become perfectly reflecting, producing a position-degenerate compact localized state. At every fixed field $0<h<h_{\rm sat}$, the singlet region remains finite as $L\to\infty$ and shrinks stepwise with increasing field, whereas at $h=0$ it spans the system.

title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
summary: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<β<4π$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.

title: Phase-Space Constraints on a General Class of Eckart-like Viscous Cosmologies
comment: LaTeX file in RevTeX 4.2 style, 18 pages, 5 figures
summary: We study the cosmological dynamics of a general class of viscous dark matter models using a dynamical system analysis. In the Eckart formalism, these viscous cosmologies are characterized by a dimensionless bulk viscous pressure $Ω_Π\equiv Ω_Π(Ω_m)$, where $Ω_m$ is the matter density parameter. Our analysis demonstrates that a viable early radiation era requires the complete absence of viscosity, a proper matter-dominated epoch demands a small viscous pressure, and the only physically admissible late-time attractor is the cosmological constant-dominated fixed point; consequently, the background expansion must closely track standard $Λ$CDM evolution. We validate these general results using the power-law parameterization $Ω_Π= -\hatξ_0 Ω_m^s$, where $\hatξ_0$ and $s$ are real parameters; for $s \geq 1$ and $\hatξ_0 \ll 1$, the model reproduces the $Λ$CDM background, while for $s < 1$ the system encounters a past-time integration boundary where the dark matter density transitions into negative values and its viscous pressure evaluates to nonphysical complex numbers. Since the background expansion essentially duplicates $Λ$CDM, the model is unlikely to resolve the $H_0$ tension. However, large differences arise at the linear perturbative level; indeed, on sub-horizon scales, bulk viscosity causes a scale-dependent dissipative drag on the matter density fluctuations; this increases the Hubble friction, offering a channel to suppress structure growth.

title: On the Energy Minimizing Problem in Plasma Dynamics
summary: A fundamental question in plasma physics and its applications to fusion theory is to find minimum energy stares of plasma.. Hong Qin has suggested the use of what he calls "Gromov ground states" which take into account the phenomenon of symplectic rigidity, as opposed to Gardner's classical approach which only use volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Howev4er Qin's approach leads to topological difficulties because his constructions remain in the classical (Hamiltonian) domain. We circumvent these difficulties by introducing a quantum-mechanical formulation of the problem, based on the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian state

title: Co layer Thickness Driven Structural Evolution and Magnetic Behaviour of Co/Ir/Co Trilayers
summary: Ferromagnetic heavy-metal (FM/HM) trilayer heterostructures provide a versatile platform for investigating the interplay between structural and magnetic properties. In this study, we investigate the effect of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of sputter-deposited $\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})/\mathrm{Ir}(5\,\mathrm{nm})/\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})$ varying from 2 to 10 nm. Structural characterization using grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals a nanocrystalline structure, with the crystallite size increasing with Co-layer thickness. Furthermore, X-ray reflectivity (XRR) reveals a thickness-dependent variation in interface morphology, with the interface roughness ratio reaching a maximum at $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 4$ nm. Temperature-dependent zero-field-cooled and field-cooled (ZFC-FC) magnetization measurements reveal thickness-dependent characteristic temperatures and multiple relaxation regimes in selected samples, indicating complex thermally activated magnetic behaviour. In contrast, field-dependent hysteresis measurements reveal that the saturation magnetization increases with Co-layer thickness, whereas the coercivity exhibits a pronounced non-monotonic variation, with enhanced values at intermediate thicknesses. Moreover, low-temperature hysteresis loops display thickness-dependent exchange-bias-like shifts, particularly for $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 2$-$4$ nm. These findings highlight the strong influence of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers.

title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
summary: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.

title: Decoupled asymmetric thin-shell wormholes
summary: We construct reflection-asymmetric thin-shell wormholes by joining a Schwarzschild exterior to its minimal geometric deformation, which shares the same mass and redshift function, so that the asymmetry is carried entirely by the gravitational-decoupling sector. The deformed side is a black hole sourced by a scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, in its branch with a real scalar. We show that the total radial null energy of shell and bulk obeys an exact identity and becomes positive for a sufficiently strong deformation. The momentum flux across the shell equals the radial null-energy density of the bulk, and retaining it yields the linear stability condition in closed form. We prove that stability with a conventional shell response requires the bulk to violate the radial null energy condition at the throat; the deformation instead enlarges the stable domain and moves the transition radius inside the photon sphere. For a stationary extension built on Kerr, the junction is solved exactly in the spin, which fixes how the angular momentum is shared between shell and bulk and where the shell behaves as a rotating fluid. A free-precession model provides an estimate of the gravitational-wave signal of the throat.

title: A Low Scale for Quark-Lepton Unification
summary: The measured fermion masses may be pointing to the scale of quark-lepton unification. Studying the renormalization-group evolution of the Standard Model Yukawa couplings, we find that $y_τ=y_b$ and $y_μ=3y_s$ occur at nearly the same scale, around $10^6$ GeV, while the first generation reaches the Georgi-Jarlskog relation $y_e\simeq y_d/3$ at order $10^8$ GeV and can arise from the same Clebsch structure through a simple hierarchical flavor texture. This pattern naturally suggests low-scale Pati-Salam symmetry. We show that flavor mixing and finite threshold corrections preserve this picture. If the electron mass has an independent origin, the two heavier-generation relations can be realized in theories with a unification scale as low as $(5$-$7)\times10^5$ GeV. We identify two simple theories that accommodate all three relations and in which the measured masses fix the flavor structure. The first unifies all three generations at $4.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\times10^6$ GeV; the second, with symmetric Yukawa matrices, at $1.5^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times10^7$ GeV, and predicts $|V_{cb}|=0.042\pm0.002$. Their shared light-family texture fixes the relevant vector-leptoquark couplings, making $μ\to e$ conversion in nuclei a direct test of unification: upcoming searches will probe part of the region selected by the two theories, and proposed facilities could cover it completely.

title: Second-Harmonic Bulk Response of Fractional Quantum Hall Fluids
summary: We develop a bulk description for the second-harmonic Hall response of fractional quantum Hall fluids with broken inversion and rotational symmetries, distinct from edge theories based on nonlinear edge-mode dispersion. By projecting a tilted massive Dirac model onto a single low-energy band, we construct a composite-boson Chern--Simons theory for the lowest Landau level that retains projection-induced nonlinear electromagnetic couplings. The nonlinear Hall resistivity vanishes in the dc limit, while its finite-frequency response retains the characteristic filling-factor dependence $ρ^{(2)}_{TLL}\proptoν^{-2}$, where $ν$ is the Landau-level filling factor. At low frequency, its real and imaginary parts scale as $(ω/ω_c)^2$ and $ω/ω_c$, respectively, where $ω_c$ is the cyclotron frequency, and the response is strongly anisotropic with respect to the crystalline tilt axis. Notably, the Kohn-mode resonances present in the second-order conductivity cancel in the nonlinear Hall resistivity. These results establish finite-frequency nonlinear transport as a bulk probe of fractional quantum Hall fluids without requiring nonlinear edge-mode dispersion.

title: Quantum dynamics on the sparse Erdős-Rényi graph
summary: We analyse the large-time asymptotics of the Schrödinger time evolution of a free quantum particle on the Erdős-Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(N,d/N)$, where the quantum Hamiltonian is given by the adjacency matrix of $\mathbb{G}$. Starting from a state localized at a vertex, the wave function is approximately radial, and we characterize precisely its asymptotic form. Our results in particular cover vertices whose degree is close to $2d$, hence probing the emergence of bound states from a dynamical perspective. This provides a dynamical counterpart of the coexistence of localized and delocalized states established in [arXiv:1905.03243,arXiv:2005.14180,arXiv:2106.12519,arXiv:2109.03227,arXiv:2305.16294], with the former giving rise to a localized mode and the latter to a dispersive wave. Our results hold in the regime $\sqrt{\log N} \ll d \ll N^{o(1)}$, which is the full region in which such dynamical phenomena may exist, and for times $1 \ll t \ll T_N$ for some explicit $T_N \gg 1$.

title: Quasibound modes of rotating acoustic black holes
summary: In this paper, we introduce a metric describing rotating acoustic black holes in spherical coordinates. This formulation allows us to obtain exact analytical solutions of the massless Klein--Gordon equation governing scalar perturbations in the corresponding background spacetime. By imposing the appropriate boundary conditions, we derive an exact analytical expression for the quasibound state frequencies of the system. Quasibound states play a central role in the dynamics of black hole analog systems, as they characterize long-lived resonant modes trapped in the vicinity of the effective horizon. Their investigation provides valuable insights into wave propagation, mode stability, and energy confinement in analog spacetimes. Moreover, because acoustic black holes offer experimentally accessible realizations of horizon physics, the study of quasibound states may establish a direct connection between theoretical predictions and laboratory observations, thereby contributing to a deeper understanding of phenomena that also arise in gravitational black hole environments.

title: Direct tests of conformal symmetry with Rydberg atoms: assessment and proposals
summary: We propose a direct test of conformal symmetry using Rydberg-atom arrays. By arranging the atoms on a circle and measuring equal-time two-point correlation functions, the characteristic functional form predicted by conformal field theory can be tested directly. We estimate the number of experimental snapshots required to resolve this behavior with sufficient statistical precision. We further optimize the time-dependent ramp profile of the Rabi frequency~$Ω$ and detuning~$Δ$ used to prepare the target critical state adiabatically. The optimized profile achieves higher fidelity over much shorter evolution times than those employed in previous experiments. Taken together, these results suggest that a direct experimental test of conformal symmetry is feasible with current Rydberg-atom technology.

title: Perpendicular Anisotropy and g-Factor of Sputtered Ni Films on Si(111) Studied by Angle-Dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance
summary: Ni films with thicknesses of 312 and 1011\,Å were grown on Si(111) by dc magnetron sputtering at room temperature and studied by atomic force microscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, X-ray reflectivity, magnetometry and angle-dependent ferromagnetic resonance. Both films are polycrystalline fcc Ni with smooth surfaces, a bulk-like (111) lattice spacing and a saturation magnetization of ${\approx}480$\,emu\,cm$^{-3}$, and both are magnetized in plane. The angular dependence of the resonance field, from the film plane to the film normal, is described by a uniaxial anisotropy model with first- and second-order terms. From this model, $g = 2.160\pm0.005$ and $2.101\pm0.014$ and effective perpendicular anisotropies of $(6.0\pm0.4)\times10^{5}$ and $(4.5\pm0.6)\times10^{5}$\,erg\,cm$^{-3}$ were obtained for the thinner and thicker film, respectively. The conventional analysis of only the in-plane and perpendicular resonances gives $g$-factors that are lower by 0.02--0.04. The perpendicular linewidths give upper limits for the Gilbert damping of $α\le 0.030$ and $\le 0.038$.

title: The diffusive spectral gap of the qubit eSWAP chain
summary: We prove that the second-moment Hamiltonian of the open qubit eSWAP chain has a diffusive spectral gap, resolving a conjecture of Li, Zheng, Liu, Jiang, and Liu. We also characterise the ground space on every connected interaction graph with at least five vertices and prove a uniform lower bound for the unnormalised complete-graph gap. We apply these results to sequential and brickwork circuits and prove that the periodic chain also has a diffusive spectral gap.

title: Gravitationally Induced Polarization-Angle Rotation in Pulsar-Black Hole Binaries
summary: Radio pulsars emit highly polarized radiation whose polarization properties are commonly described by the Rotating Vector Model (RVM). In this work, we investigate the effects of gravitational light bending and parallel transport on the polarization profile of a pulsar in a hypothetical binary system with a black hole (BH) companion. We combine the RVM with numerical integration of null geodesics to calculate the polarization direction along the photon trajectory and model the orbital-phase-dependent variation of the observed polarization position angle (PPA). We consider both non-spinning and spinning black hole companions and include the evolution of the orbital geometry due to relativistic spin-orbit coupling. For a non-spinning black hole, the change in the observed polarization direction arises from the geometric shift associated with gravitational light bending. For a spinning black hole, frame dragging introduces an additional geometric shift, while parallel transport produces an additional polarization rotation measured relative to our chosen reference construction. We investigate the dependence of these polarization changes on the binary parameters and the orientation of the pulsar spin. We find that gravitational light bending can significantly distort the characteristic S-shaped PPA profile, particularly near superior conjunction, and can reverse its overall sense of variation for the supermassive black hole system considered here. Relativistic spin-orbit evolution also affects the orbital-phase dependence of the polarization profile, particularly in the supermassive black hole system. These results show that relativistic photon propagation can modify both the shape and the phase dependence of pulsar polarization profiles and may provide a useful probe of the geometry of pulsar-BH binaries when such systems are discovered.

title: A new analytical finding for the Born-Infeld integral potential
summary: A new finding regarding the Born-Infeld potential for short range distances from the charge revealed that its integral form can be almost exact written as the difference between a Coulomb-type potential and a Yukawa-type potential. This allowed for an immediate physical interpretation in terms of classical vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Subsequently, a new U(r) is proposed to cover the entire space. This formulation is then applied to calculate, in a closed manner, the first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms; a comparison of these shifts with high-precision spectroscopic data provides a model-dependent lower bound for the maximum field intensity parameter b.

title: Effect of niobium doping on the local structure and oxidation state of Co atoms in SrTiO$_3$
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables; authors' translation to appear in Physics of the Solid State
summary: XAFS spectroscopy combined with first-principles calculations are used to study SrTiO$_3$ samples simultaneously doped with cobalt and niobium. It is shown that additional doping of the samples with Nb donors results in a decrease in the oxidation state of cobalt atoms to +2, which is accompanied by an increase in the Co--O distance to the nearest oxygen atoms, in agreement with first-principles calculations. The impurity Co atoms are shown to occupy Ti sites and are on-center. The suppression of the oxygen-vacancy formation upon doping SrTiO$_3$(Co) with niobium was revealed. First-principles calculations indicate that the Coulomb interaction of ions with local electric fields generated by non-isoelectronic Nb impurities plays a decisive role in the local distortions of atomic positions observed around the cobalt atom in the unit cell. The possibility of controlling the magnetic moment of Co atoms by intentional change in the lattice parameter is demonstrated.

title: Spatial symmetry invariance of three-dimensional Navier-Stokes turbulence
summary: Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) of the deterministic Navier-Stokes (NS) equations is widely used to provide benchmark solutions of turbulent flow, but its accuracy and reliability have not been rigorously inspected from a mathematical viewpoint. Here we prove a spatial symmetry invariance theorem (SSIT) of three-dimensional NS equations whereby an exact solution of deterministic NS equations under periodic boundary conditions maintains the same spatial symmetry as its symmetric initial flow, forever. SSIT provides an absolute benchmark test for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). It is shown herein that traditional DNS of NS turbulence quickly violates SSIT, revealing that the spatiotemporal trajectory of NS turbulence predicted by DNS soon becomes badly polluted by numerical noise. Importantly, it is found that even the statistical results of DNS might be unstable, i.e., exhibit sensitivity dependence on the initial flow conditions. In other words, the loss of spatial symmetry in traditional DNS of NS turbulence is not a physical instability but instead a numerical artifact caused by the chaotic nature of the flow. Using the SSIT, it is straightforward to deduce several key properties of NS turbulence, including `ultra-chaos', the so-called `noise-expansion cascade', `permanent memory of symmetric initial flow conditions', and so on. Note that permanent memory of symmetric initial flow conditions suggests that NS turbulence governed by deterministic NS equations subject to symmetric initial flow should have no `mixing', corresponding to non-ergodicity, although ergodicity is one of the most fundamental assumptions of turbulence theory.

title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
summary: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

title: Hitchin's $α$-invariant and positive sectional curvature on homotopy $9$-spheres
summary: We prove that a smooth homotopy $9$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature if and only if its Hitchin $α$-invariant vanishes, or equivalently if and only if it admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.

title: Aging dynamics and generalized superposition principles in carbon black-carboxymethylcellulose hydrogels
summary: Aqueous dispersions of hydrophobic carbon black (CB) particles can be stabilized by carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), forming CB-CMC hydrogels whose microstructure is controlled by the relative CB-to-polymer content. At low CMC content, CB particles form a percolated, electrically conductive network, whereas at higher polymer content, CB particles act as isolated physical crosslinkers within an electrically insulating polymer matrix [see Legrand \textit{et al.}, Macromolecules 56, 2298-2308 (2023)]. Combining rheology and electrical impedance spectroscopy, we show that these two regimes exhibit markedly different aging dynamics. Conductive hydrogels exhibit logarithmic elastic recovery associated with a percolated CB network, whereas insulating hydrogels exhibit a combination of logarithmic and power-law stiffening, accompanied by dielectric polarization associated with confined ionic motion. The insulating hydrogels further exhibit a time-aging superposition principle, as their viscoelastic spectra measured in a time-resolved fashion can collapse onto a single master curve. Under steady shear, the viscoelastic response measured perpendicular to the flow also obeys a time--shear-rate superposition principle. Remarkably, the scaling between the shift factors under shear is reminiscent of critical-gel behavior, unlike that observed during aging at rest. Finally, time-resolved rheo-USAXS measurements performed during shear-rate cycles reveal structural rearrangements of CB particles and clusters that correlate with rheological hysteresis. These results provide a microstructural basis for understanding the nonlinear rheology of insulating CB-CMC hydrogels and establish generalized superposition principles as a unifying framework for their aging and flow behavior.

title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
summary: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.

title: Lunar tidal response-induced clock frequency variations on the Moon
summary: As clock performance improves, the instability and uncertainty of the clock's fractional frequency shift (FFS) become comparable to the FFS caused by the lunar tidal response (LTR), so the influence of the LTR on lunar time needs to be investigated. In this paper, we used the Keplerian expansions method to study the FFS to the level of $10^{-18}$ caused by the LTR between two clocks placed in different positions on the Moon. We consider the case of the Moon orbiting in an elliptical orbit, which is closer to the actual situation compared to the case of the Moon moving in a circular orbit. An interesting phenomenon is found that the longitude difference between two clocks can cause a change in the amplitude and phase of the FFS due to the LTR, but the latitude difference only changes the amplitude of the FFS. We further estimated the clock difference between two clocks near the Moon caused by the LTR. When one clock is on the lunar surface, and the other is on the Earth's surface, the LTR will cause a clock difference of $% -5.68\times 10^{-7}$ $μ$s/day between the two clocks. These are significant for the construction of a lunar time and clock synchronization near the Moon.

title: Acoustic Schwarzschild-like black hole and analogous Hawking radiation in Einstein-bumblebee gravity
summary: We derive an acoustic Schwarzschild-like black hole and study its analogous Hawking radiation in Einstein-bumblebee theory by using Gross-Pitaevskii theory in the background of Schwarzschild-like spacetime. This black hole have two kinds of event horizons: one is the gravitational horizon $r_h=2M$(black hole horizon), the others are the internal and external acoustic horizons $2M<r_{ac-}\leq4M,\;r_{ac}\geq4M$(dumb hole horizon) which depend on the tuning parameter $ξ$ and Lorentz violation coupling constant $\ell$. The corresponding Hawking temperature $T_h$ depends only on $\ell$, however $T_{ac}$ depends on $\ell$ and $ξ$. The dumb hole temperature $T_{ac}$ has a maximum $T_{acm}=T_h/8$. When considering the scalar particles radiating from the dumb hole, we find that in low frequency, the grey-body factor increases with the tuning parameter $ξ$, but decreases with $\ell$. In the high frequency, it approaches to $1$. Its energy emission rate is similar to the Planck's black spectrum where there has a maximum at a given peak frequency $ω_m$. The energy emission rate also increases with the tuning parameter $ξ$, but decreases with $\ell$. This opposite dependence relationship is the most experimentally valuable feature and can directly benchmark against observations of real astrophysical black holes.

title: Harnessing Electrostructural Bistability to Control Defects in Polarizable Materials
summary: Structural defects are central to the functionalities of materials. However, conventional approaches to defect control are often slow and imprecise. This work identifies and characterizes a distinct physical phenomenon of electrostructural bistability that provides a rapid and precise pathway for engineering materials with defect-controlled physical properties. A generalized theory of conductivity bistability is developed and experimentally validated to unify two distinct regimes: previously reported electrothermal bistability in weakly polarizable insulators, such as silicon, and electrostructural bistability in strongly polarizable materials, such as TiO$_2$. In agreement with the theory, experiments on TiO$_2$ demonstrate that bulk-homogeneous defect concentrations in electrostructurally bistable materials can be tuned rapidly and deterministically by controlling applied electric current. Abruptly interrupting the current quenches the system into long-lived, room-temperature metastable states with distinct properties. This establishes a practical, rapid, and scalable pathway for defect engineering with direct relevance to nonvolatile memory devices.

title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index
summary: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.

title: On the Doppler Effect in Static Materials: Vortices and Black, White and Worm-Hole Like Wave Trajectories
summary: We demonstrate the Doppler effect in a static material. The effect is achieved with a network of thin waveguides whose lengths depend on the direction of travel, chosen to simulate the compression and expansion of the wave experienced by a source travelling with velocity $v$. Each edge of length $\ell$ becomes a pair of waveguides of lengths $\ell/(1\mp v/c)$, one for each direction of travel. On a lattice this gives the field pattern of a moving source. To demonstrate the effect, we design a vortex, an analogue black hole and wormhole.

title: Krylov geometry and optimal recovery under uncertain coherent noise
summary: Recovery from a coherent rotation with an unobserved angle depends on both the encoding and what calibration reveals about the noise. We determine their combined limit for a known finite-dimensional generator and one final recovery. Two polynomial projections organize the answer. A physical Krylov chain separates correctable error amplitudes from their first state-dependent distortion; projection onto lower-angle powers identifies the part that a coherent decoder can cancel. Under explicit rank and moment conditions, their combination gives the exact leading optimal entanglement infidelity at weak noise and a recovery attaining it for any finite logical dimension. The optimal worst-input error lies between one and $d$ times that infidelity at leading order, for logical dimension $d$. When the angle distribution is unknown, we optimize one decoder for every distribution compatible with the calibration. When spectral and calibration frequencies are integer multiples of a common frequency, moment positivity turns this into an exact finite optimization. Small measured means can still allow rare finite rotations. If the sole calibration datum is $β_r=\mathbb E[\sin^{2r}(θ/2)]$, with $θ$ the wrapped rotation phase at that common frequency, the optimal worst-prior infidelity is $O(β_r)$ exactly when generator powers through degree $r-1$ are correctable. When the first uncorrectable power has degree $m<r$, the optimal loss scales as $β_r^{m/r}$, with a sharp coefficient fixed by a universal moment problem. In a loss-free four-photon memory, population measurements at two calibration durations retain the fully informed quartic error coefficient for a fixed symmetric narrow-noise family with positive variance and finite fourth moment; a single duration permits loss quadratic in the noise width.

title: Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
summary: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? We investigate this possibility in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with repulsive Coulomb interactions. Self-consistent Hartree--Fock calculations identify a commensurate triangular Wigner-crystal state. To investigate pairing on the metallic side, we construct a crossing-symmetric particle--hole vertex using coupled parquet and Bethe--Salpeter equations, incorporating exchange vertex corrections beyond polarization-bubble screening. Near crystallization, the enhanced electronic correlations generate an effective attraction favoring chiral $f$-wave pairing. Superconductivity is confined to a narrow metallic region adjacent to the crystal, qualitatively consistent with the superconducting sleeve observed near an insulating regime in rhombohedral graphene. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

title: A New Non-Affine Family in the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection
summary: We show that $K_6^{(2)} \cap X_6^{(2)} = D_6^{(1)} \cup C_6^{(1)}$ up to standard Hadamard equivalence, where $C_6^{(1)}$ is a new non-affine one-parameter family of complex Hadamard matrices. This demonstrates that the intersection of the two-parameter Hadamard families of Karlsson and Szöllősi is strictly larger than the known affine Diţă curve $D_6^{(1)}$. Our new parametrisation of the Szöllősi family $X_6^{(2)}$ in Karlsson coordinates and our constructive classification of the Karlsson-Szöllősi intersection shed light on the intersection of block-reducible forms and hypocycloid constraints. This may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions.

title: Dark Matter phase space distribution under a fully relativistic treatment. Eddington inversion according to general relativity
summary: We develop a fully relativistic extension of Eddington inversion to reconstruct the phase-space distribution function of dark matter from its density profile. Treating dark matter as an effective perfect fluid in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime, we use the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to determine the gravitational background and derive an Abel-type inversion that yields the distribution function in terms of the conserved particle energy measured at infinity. We show that the resulting expression recovers the classical Eddington inversion in the weak-field, nonrelativistic limit. We also investigate the finite-boundary contribution, which can introduce an unphysical divergence, and present a regularization procedure that removes it. We apply our method to a Milky Way model consisting of a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White halo and a Gondolo-Silk dark-matter spike around Sagittarius A$^*$, neglecting baryonic contributions. The relativistic and Newtonian velocity distributions agree at radii far from the Galactic center but begin to differ at distances of order $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{pc}$. Closer to the black hole, the relativistic peak speed can reach approximately twice the Newtonian prediction. Finally, we derive a general expression for dark-matter capture by neutron stars that accommodates arbitrary ambient velocity distributions. Near Sagittarius A$^*$, the relativistic capture factor is nearly an order of magnitude smaller than the Maxwell-Boltzmann prediction, while the Newtonian Eddington result can overestimate it by a factor of approximately two. These results demonstrate the importance of relativistic phase-space reconstruction for dark-matter phenomenology in strong gravitational fields.

title: Spectroscopy of the SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
comment: 29 pages, 11 figures, 12 tables; submission to SciPost
summary: We investigate the ground state spectrum of a dynamical scalar-fermion-gauge system with an SU(2) gauge group, a scalar doublet, and two degenerate generations of vectorial fermions under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect. To this end, we employ lattice methods using the HiRep code. We study the dependence of the system on the (bare) fermion mass and find that the spectrum remains unaffected, up to trivial fermion mass effects. The results are in line with a weakly coupled theory exhibiting the Fröhlich-Morchio-Strocchi mechanism.

title: Scattering and Schmid-Bulgadaev Transition in Qubits Based on Josephson Junction Chains
summary: A Josephson junction subject to an ohmic dissipative environment undergoes a zero-temperature quantum phase transition called Schmid-Bulgadaev transition form an insulating state to a superconducting state upon increasing the impedance of the environment above the resistance quantum. Superconducting qubits based on Josephson junction chains represent a system where it is possible to dynamically explore both sides of this transition by probing the scattering of individual plasma modes of the junction chain on a SQUID at the boundary which was achieved in recent experiments. Here, we provide a theoretical analysis of the scattering in the system paying special attention to the non-perturbative superconducting regime. We find that in this regime, a specific diagrammatic resummation must be performed in order to correctly account for fluctuation renormalization of the SQUID's potential. We find analytic expressions for the modes' frequency shifts and quality factors which together provide a full description of scattering. We argue that the non-perturbative nature of the superconducting phase manifests itself through a power-law dependence of the frequency shifts on the SQUID flux and through non-monotonous dependence of the quality factors on the mode frequency. Our predictions may be readily verified in modern low-temperature experiments.

title: Hyperboloidal Initial Data with Prescribed Asymptotic Charges
summary: A novel method is introduced for constructing hyperboloidal initial data with direct analytic control over asymptotic charges prior to solving the Einstein constraint equations. Using the parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the constraints together with a Fuchsian-analysis-inspired spectral solver, the asymptotic degrees of freedom, which determine infinite towers of asymptotic charges, including the Bondi energy and angular momentum, are used to prescribe the asymptotic behavior of solutions. As a proof of concept, we explicitly construct hyperboloidal initial data for a spinning black hole with Bondi energy $E_B = 2$ and angular momentum $J_B = 1/2$, starting from seed data induced on a hyperboloidal slice of the non-rotating Schwarzschild spacetime with mass $M=1$.

title: The Hosts and Mass Distribution Function of the Most Massive Black Holes: Implications for the nHz Gravitational Wave Background
comment: 29 pages, 15 figures, submitted to the Astrophysical Journal
summary: We use the core-radius, $r_γ,$ of a galaxy's central core along with a volume-limited sample of brightest cluster galaxies (BCG) to determine the $z=0$ mass distribution function of the most massive super-massive black holes (SMBH). We recover a $M_{BH}-r_γ$ relationship between the SMBH mass, $M_{BH},$ and $r_γ$ of form $M_{BH} \approx1.3\times10^{10}~(r_γ/{\mathrm{kpc}})~M_\odot,$ with $σ= 0.25\pm0.03$ dex scatter in $M_{BH}.$ We derive a core distribution function (CDF), based on HST and DLS images of the BCGs. The CDF falls steeply as $N(r_γ)\sim r_γ^{-3}$ for $r_γ>0.50$ kpc. Only $\sim5\%$ of BCGs have $r_γ>1$ kpc. Combining the CDF and $M_{BH} - r_γ$ relationship yields the BH mass distribution function (MDF). For $M_{BH} \geq 7\times10^{9}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ (the mean $M_{BH}$ at $r_γ=0.50$ kpc) we derive: $\log\left(\frac{dN(M_{BH})}{d{M_{BH}/10^{10} M_\odot}}~[\rm Mpc^{-3}]\right)=(-3.05\pm0.42)~\log\left(\frac{M_{BH}}{10^{10}M_\odot}\right)~-~5.11\ (+0.41, -0.36)$. Cores with $r_γ\geq 0.50$ kpc are found almost exclusively in BCGs, implying that SMBHs with $M_{BH} \geq7\times10^{9}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ may also be exclusive to BCGs. Core-radius correlates with $α,$ a parameter that characterizes the growth of BCG envelopes by mergers, suggesting that the most massive SMBHs grew in tandem with their BCG hosts. The BH MDF embodies a significant population of SMBH with $M_{BH} >7\times10^{9} M_\odot.$ When combined with the Liepold & Ma (2024) BH MDF to account for SMBH with $M_{BH} < 7\times10^{9} M_\odot,$ it can comfortably explain the nHz gravitational wave background.

title: Induced Bell-CHSH observables in the Fewster-Verch measurement scheme
summary: The Summers-Werner theorem shows that the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory violates the Bell-CHSH inequality maximally on complementary wedges, but it is an existence statement: it exhibits neither the observables nor an apparatus that measures them. We give an explicit operator-level realization within the Fewster-Verch measurement framework, obtaining dichotomic Bell observables of a free Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions as observables induced by local couplings to Majorana probes. The induced system smearing factorizes exactly as $f_h=k\,b_{λ,h}$, so its support is controlled by the compactly supported coupling profile $k$; dichotomy is imposed by calibrating and normalizing the induced smearings rather than required of the probe observable; and a probe-only normal ordering yields the product of Alice's and Bob's induced bilinears, which the non-multiplicative induced map alone does not provide. Under explicit attainability hypotheses the induced observables saturate the Tsirelson bound in a state prepared from the vacuum. The construction extends to coupled scalar fields.

title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
summary: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
summary: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.

title: Quantum-Relativistic Anomalous Proper Time
summary: We investigate surprising consequences of the hypothesis that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle. We show that, for a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, the elapsed proper time in another region of space can assume an anomalous effective value lying outside the range allowed by classical general relativity. Remarkably, the effective elapsed proper time can even become negative, corresponding to an effective evolution backward in time. We also propose an experiment to observe an anomalous effective proper time associated with the internal degrees of freedom of a quantum particle in an interferometer under Earth's gravitational field. The proposed experiment is, in principle, feasible with current technology, and its realization could provide the first experimental evidence of an interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity beyond the effects of the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.

title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
comment: Detailed QNM and QBS scan results are tabulated in Appendix D
summary: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics. It provides an exact solution of Einstein gravity and admits a finite completion. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. In this setup, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

title: First-Principles-Informed Modeling of Thermal Transport and Laser-Induced Heating in Ultrahigh-Temperature Carbides
summary: Using first-principles density functional theory and Boltzmann transport calculations, we systematically investigate the electronic structure, lattice and electronic thermal transport, optical response, and laser-induced heating of ultrahigh-temperature carbides (UHTCs), including Group IV (TiC, ZrC, and HfC) and Group V carbides (VC, NbC, and TaC), and SiC. The transition-metal carbides (TMCs) exhibit metallic electronic structures, whereas SiC exhibits semiconducting character. The calculated thermal transport properties reveal distinct contributions from phonons and electrons, with electronic heat transport becoming increasingly important at elevated temperatures in TMCs. The Group V carbides exhibit substantially lower lattice thermal conductivity than their Group IV counterparts, accompanied by pronounced Kohn anomalies and modified phonon dispersions associated with their distinct electronic structures, suggesting a possible connection between Fermi-surface topology, phonon dynamics, and lattice thermal transport. In contrast, SiC exhibits comparatively high lattice thermal conductivity, consistent with its long-lived acoustic phonons, but no electronic contribution due to its semiconducting nature. Optical calculations reveal relatively high reflectivity in the visible and infrared spectral ranges for the metallic carbides, whereas SiC exhibits lower reflectivity in the infrared region. Finally, one-dimensional and three-dimensional continuum heat-conduction models are employed to compare the thermal responses of these materials under specified laser irradiation conditions. The predicted temperature distributions depend on the thermal and optical properties of the materials as well as the specimen geometry.

title: Semiclassical dynamics of higher-order squeezing: self-adjoint extensions and coherent returns
summary: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians have several self-adjoint realizations, while their classical trajectories reach infinity in finite time. We relate these extension problems through boundary amplitudes and the semiclassical propagation of coherent states. A discrete Fourier transformation gives the sink-to-source ray matrix of each quantum realization. After the first passage through infinity, the full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, with weights equal to the squared moduli of the matrix entries. The proof combines finite-order approximate tail solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition with full-norm Gaussian matching and a square-summable residual estimate. For positive energy, we determine the limit after any fixed number of passages: amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix. We also realize these limits by concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension, distinguishing deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.

title: Initial Data Gluing for Asymptotically Hyperbolic Spacetimes
summary: We give a new proof of Corvino-Schoen-type gluing, also known as gluing up to linear obstructions, for asymptotically hyperbolic spacetimes satisfying appropriate smallness conditions in arbitrary dimension. The results retrieve and improve on previous known smallness requirements on initial data to conduct such gluing, including the work of Chrusciél and Delay. Our technique is highly versatile and well-suited for gluing results in highly anisotropic geometric settings.

title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
summary: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.

title: Annealing-atmosphere control of paramagnetic defects in ZnO microparticles
summary: In this work, we used temperature-dependent electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to reveal the effect of high-temperature annealing in N2 and air on paramagnetic and electronic properties of ZnO microparticles. EPR spectral simulations have shown that N2 annealing produces Zni, VO+, and shallow-donor centers, whereas Zni, VO+, and Hi-related centers are observed after annealing the ZnO microparticles in an air atmosphere. The resolved paramagnetic centers exhibit distinctly different behavior over 5-297 K. The shallow-donor and Hi signals are rapidly quenched below approximately 50 K, while the Zni contribution shows a nonmonotonic temperature dependence. In contrast, the VO+ signal persists up to room temperature and increases with temperature, consistent with charge redistribution among donor-related defects involving deep oxygen-vacancy states. The cavity Q-factor generally decreases with increasing temperature for both annealed samples, indicating atmosphere-dependent changes in the microwave losses. These results show that the annealing atmosphere controls the paramagnetic defect population, the temperature dependence of donor-related centers, and the associated electronic response of ZnO microparticles.

title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
comment: 25 pages, 7 figures. This preprint supersedes the earlier preprint arXiv:2001.01295
summary: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+λ^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $λ$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.

title: Catastrophe Structure and Stability of Axion Stars
summary: Axion stars are self-gravitating Bose--Einstein condensates of QCD axions or axion-like particles. Their stability determines whether they can survive as dark-matter structures and what astrophysical signatures they may produce. Here we combine a non-relativistic Schrödinger--Poisson description with catastrophe theory to develop a unified picture of axion-star stability. Beginning with the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system for a periodic axion potential, we derive the effective equations of motion and conserved quantities and construct a one-parameter family of star-like solutions. A Gaussian variational ansatz reduces the problem to an analytic energy functional $E(R;N)$. Within this model, equilibria appear and disappear through Arnold $A_2$, $A_3$, and $A_4$ catastrophes as the particle number $N$ and interaction strengths vary. A repulsive sextic interaction produces two stable branches---dilute and dense axion stars---separated by an unstable branch. The same catastrophe criteria apply beyond the sextic truncation: for the full cosine and QCD-corrected potentials, the fold conditions follow from the complete variational energy and can be evaluated numerically. We also separate stability within the collective-coordinate ansatz from full radial perturbative stability and specify the range in which the non-relativistic treatment is reliable. This framework provides a compact classification of axion-star phases and identifies model-dependent critical masses associated with collapse, bosenova-like emission, and black-hole formation.

title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
summary:
We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response.
  By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.

title: Momentum-selective graphene spectroscopy of moiré excitons
summary: Far-field photoluminescence probes only the light-cone corner of an exciton's momentum content, whereas energy transfer to nearby graphene integrates in-plane momenta up to the inverse spacer thickness $1/z$. For a WSe$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterobilayer we build the transition polarization $\bm{P}_n(\qv)$ of each localized moiré exciton from the registry-dependent vector dipole texture and use each $\bm{P}_n$ for both baths. The two baths rank the states differently: the graphene-rate ratios differ from the optical ones, their ordering inverts with spacer thickness, and the distance exponents at $z=10$\,nm spread by more than two units. These ratios are independent of the transition-dipole prefactor. Within the $C_3$-symmetric leading-harmonic model the chiral $p_+$ and $d_-$ states are also dark at normal incidence yet transfer to graphene at rates comparable to the bright ground state. Their graphene rate depends on the sign of the texture phase, a quantity invisible in far-field emission, which we determine from first principles. In a device this prediction requires a splitting, larger than the symmetry-breaking mixing, that protects the chiral partners. Graphene proximity thus acts as a momentum-selective near-field probe of moiré excitons, and we propose its use as a practical spectroscopy.

title: Six-Degree-of-Freedom Rotor-Load Cross-Spectral Density from Rotor-Plane Turbulence Cross-Spectra
summary: A frequency-domain response analysis of a wind turbine rotor requires the complete hub-load spectrum, but the customary scalar thrust and torque spectra retain neither the four in-plane components nor the coupling between them. This paper derives the full six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) rotor-load cross-spectral-density (CSD) matrix from the IEC Kaimal turbulence model. By decoupling the spatial order of inflow coherence from the temporal Doppler shift, the formulation introduces a two-index rotational-sampling kernel. Rotor symmetry and azimuthal averaging constrain the observed Doppler carrier strictly to blade-passing harmonics $pBf_{\mathrm{rot}}$, while the azimuthal aerodynamic transfer shifts the spatial coherence order to $pB+s$. A convergence study of the retained azimuthal order $s$ shows that $\lvert s\rvert\le4$ suffices, the assembled CSD then deviating from the full-band result by less than $10^{-5}$ in relative norm. The formulation is compared with OpenFAST simulations of a rigid floating wind turbine over nine wind speeds: the six auto-spectral densities agree closely below 1~Hz, and the present theory over-predicts the spectra near the 6P and 9P rotational harmonics.

title: Price's law for scalar waves on 1+4 dimensional subextremal Myers-Perry spacetimes
summary:
We consider Myers--Perry spacetimes $(M,g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}})$ in $1+4$ dimensions with two spin parameters $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})\in\mathbb{R}^2$, which are a direct generalization of the well known Kerr spacetime in $1+3$ dimensions. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow associated to $g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}$ is normally hyperbolically trapped for the full subextremal range \[
  (|\mathbf{a}|+|\mathbf{b}|)^2<2\mathfrak{m}. \] As an application, we prove a Price law with explicit leading order terms for solutions $φ(t,x)$ of the scalar wave equation \[
  \Box_{g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}}φ=0 \] under the assumption of real mode stability. Our precise asymptotics imply that $φ(t,x)=ct^{-3}+\mathcal{O}(t^{-4+})$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ is an explicitly computable constant.

title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
summary: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions.
