However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.

title: kstress: a LAMMPS package for calculating the 2D wavevector-dependent stress tensor and its anisotropy in amorphous solids
summary: The stress tensor resolved in wavevector $\qvec$ and time $t$, $σ_{αβ}(\qvec,t)$, gives access to the elastic moduli of amorphous solids as a function of the probed length scale, and to the long-range stress correlations that distinguish an amorphous solid from a liquid. Its evaluation requires the contribution of every interacting pair and therefore an interface to the force loop of the molecular dynamics code. In the current work, we present: i) an optimized implementation of the LAMMPS~\cite{lammps} module for calculating $σ_{αβ}(\qvec,t)$, in which trigonometric functions are calculated only for the basic wavevectors and, in addition, all the relevant wavevectors are supplied as an explicit list rather than generated as a full grid, so that only the wavevectors of interest are computed and stored, and ii) a validation protocol for the code illustrated for a two-dimensional polydisperse Lennard-Jones (2DpLJ) glass-forming liquid. Based on these technical achievements we elucidated how the affine moduli for the 2DpLJ model depend on the norm $q$ of the wavevector. In particular, we demonstrate that the longitudinal affine modulus shows a minimum near $q_\text{max}$ corresponding to the main peak of the structure factor. Our data also point to the peaks in the $q$-dependencies of vibrational frequencies well below $q_\text{max}$ for both transverse and longitudinal modes. The potential relevance of this feature to the ``boson peak'' is discussed as well.

title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
summary: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $Λ$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $σ$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(σ)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $aΛ\log(1/(aΛ))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(Λ,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(aΛ))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.

title: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain
summary:
Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model $H=\sum_j\{\boldsymbol S_j\cdot\boldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_j^{\mathrm z})^2\}$ for sufficiently small $|D|$. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the $\mathrm z$ direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in $D$ on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on $D$. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper.
  The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.

title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
summary: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.

title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
summary: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
summary: Theoretical modelling of diamond growth should ideally provide estimates of the growth rate depending on experimental conditions. To that end, a description of all possible reactions related to the competing adsorption, desorption and migration mechanisms is required. Here, we provide precise calculations of the reaction rate coefficient of methyl-related reactions on hydrogen-terminated (100) diamond surface, as $\mathrm{CH_3}$ is known to be the main growth precursor in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of diamond. To achieve this goal, we successfully combined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and variational transition state theory (VTST), allowing to extend our analysis to barrierless reaction. Our rigorous treatment of the quasi-free rotation of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ adsorbates on the surface allows us to overcome numerical errors for the finite difference calculations of the vibrational spectra for evaluating the partition functions of the system. Our results suggest that the mechanism that deplete the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ concentration the most is the absorption on a surface radical site. We also evidence the anisotropy of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ migration along the dimer of the (100)-(2x1):H surface. In a more general perspective, the calculated reaction rates coefficient for methyl reactions and migration presented in this work, together with the data for hydrogen reaction and other main gas surface reactions, bridge the gap between the atomic-scale description and the large-scale modelling of diamond growth.

title: Physical Adjoint Learning in Wave Systems with Asymmetric Couplings
comment: Main text: 13 pages, 7 figures; (+) Supplementary Information: 5 pages, 1 figure
summary: Developing self-optimizing physical systems that learn directly from their response to external stimuli offers a promising route toward adaptive and intelligent machines. A key ingredient is the ability to evaluate optimization gradients within the physical hardware, bypassing the need for accurate numerical models. In wave systems, \textit{in-situ} adjoint methods provide this capability by exploiting reciprocity to physically realize the adjoint dynamics. However, this approach generally breaks down in nonreciprocal systems, where the adjoint field cannot be directly accessed through the original device. Here, we develop an \textit{in-situ} adjoint optimization framework that extends physical gradient computation to wave systems with asymmetric couplings through computationally low-cost similarity transformations between the forward and transposed operators. We utilize available degrees of freedom like tailored injected excitations, targeted measurements, and tunable parameters, to enable adjoint field reconstruction through forward experiments on the same physical platform. We demonstrate the versatility of the protocol through broadband transmission and isolation, coherent perfect absorption, programmable wavefront shaping, and spatially selective sensing. Our results provide a route to self-optimization in complex nonreciprocal wave systems through efficient physical gradient-based learning. The number of experiments required by the protocol does not increase with the number of optimization parameters, and the method remains applicable even when parts of the system are completely inaccessible.

title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
summary: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

title: The mathematical journey of spatial reciprocity
summary: Over the past three decades, evolutionary game theory in structured populations has witnessed explosive progress. Counterintuitive cooperative phenomena discovered in simulations have stimulated the development of rigorous mathematical theories to describe the underlying dynamics. In this paper, we review these theoretical advancements, including pair approximation and coalescent theory, which offer analytical solutions to evolutionary games on networks. We summarize the key results obtained by these theories, while also discussing their limitations, such as high computational complexity and constrained flexibility when applied to complex models. We therefore suggest that mathematical approaches provide a complementary tool for understanding cooperation in structured populations alongside simulations.

title: External-field-modified entropic exchange in confined quantum systems: static versus time-dependent electric fields
summary: We review how external electric fields reshape the information content of spatially confined atoms, and we contrast the response to a uniform static field with that to a monochromatic, time-dependent laser field. The central quantities are the Shannon entropies in position and momentum space, Sr and Sp, and their sum ST = Sr +Sp, which obeys the BBM bound. Using the confined hydrogen atom (CHA) and the particle in a spherical box (PISB), its tight confinement limit, as reference systems, we first show that the field-free total entropy of the CHA depends non-monotonically on the confining radius whereas that of the PISB is strictly scale invariant. We then present Stark maps of the entropies for the ten lowest m = 0 levels at the confining radius of 6 a.u. The ground-state polarizability is reduced from the free-atom value 4.5 a.u. to 4.06 a.u. in the CHA but is 46.8 a.u. in the PISB, and the entropic response of the two systems differs correspondingly.

title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
summary: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.

title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
summary: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.

title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
summary: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power $p$ close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength $W$ of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power $p_1$ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with $p<0$ on an interval around $E = 1$ spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E = \infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E)=-1$ for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength $W$ rather than the lattice size $L$.

title: Quantum state revivals, time quasicrystals, and entanglement steering in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model
summary: Motivated by the search for non-equilibrium phases of matter beyond the Floquet paradigm, we propose a route to realize perfect revivals and time quasicrystals (TQCs) in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model with Ising interactions between the central and satellite spins in the absence of disorder. We analytically demonstrate that when the interaction strength, $λ$ is tuned to $2 m π$, no entanglement is generated between the central and satellite spins at stroboscopic times, independent of the strength of the transverse driving field and the drive sequence. This leads to indefinitely long-lived quasiperiodic oscillations in satellite spin magnetization. Furthermore, for initial states with a definite bath magnetization, no entanglement is generated when the transverse driving field, $θ$ is tuned to $π$ for any value of $ λ$, and the satellite spin magnetization oscillations exhibit period-3 revivals at Fibonacci times. Examining the robustness of these oscillations away from this fine-tuned limit, we identify a parameter regime where the quasiperiodic response does not decay over the timescales probed, giving rise to a long-lived $π$-pulse-proximate TQC regime. We further show that at special Clifford points, the system exhibits perfect quasiperiodic oscillations of the satellite spin magnetization, with a parity-dependent Fourier response. This response persists over the timescales probed, even away from the Clifford points for an even number of satellite spins, leading to the formation of a Clifford-proximate TQC. Finally, we demonstrate that at this Clifford points, the system is steered along an entangled trajectory, leading to the dynamical generation of Bell-cat and spin-cat states. These states exhibit magnetization of collective spin fluctuates quadratically with the number of satellite spins, thereby enabling Heisenberg-limited metrology.

title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
summary: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.

title: Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
summary: Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.

title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
summary: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.

title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
comment: 7pages, 4 figures, with supplemental materials 14 pages, 4 figures
summary: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
summary: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.
